statement.p: Let R be the rectangle with vertices (0,0), (2,0), (2,2), and (0,2) and let f(x,y) = \sqrt{4xy}.
(a) Find reasonable upper and lower bounds for \int_{R}f\,dA without subdividing R.

(b) Estimate \int_{R}f\,dA three ways: by partitioning R into four subrectangles and evaluating f at its maximum and minimum values on each subrectangle, and then by considering the average of these (over and under) estimates.

static.solution:
(a) If we take the partition of R consisting of just R itself, we get \mbox{Lower bound }= \mbox{min}_R f\cdot A_R=0\cdot (2-0)(2-0)=0. Similarly, we get \mbox{Upper bound } = \hbox{max}_R f\cdot A_R = 4\cdot (2-0)(2-0)=16.
(b) The estimates asked for are just the upper and lower sums. We partition R into subrectangles R_{(a,b)} of width 1 and height 1, where (a,b) is the lower-left corner of R_{(a,b)}. The subrectangles are then R_{(0,0)}, R_{(1,0)}, R_{(0,2)}, and R_{(2,2)}. Then we find the lower sum \mbox{Lower } =\sum_{(a,b)}A_{R_{(a,b)}}\cdot\min_{R_{(a,b)}}f = \sum_{(a,b)} 1\cdot (\mbox{Min of }f \mbox{ on }R_{(a,b)}). The minimum occurs at the lower-left corner of each rectangle, so \mbox{Lower } = 1\cdot( f(0,0) + f(1,0) + f(0,1) + f(1,1) ) = 16.
Similarly, the upper sum is \mbox{Upper } = 1\sum_{(a,b)}(\mbox{Max of }f \mbox{ on }R_{(a,b)}), so \mbox{Upper } = 1(f(2,2)+f(4,2)+f(2,4)+f(4,4)) = 1(6 + 2\sqrt2). The upper sum is an overestimate and the lower sum is an underestimate, so we can get a better estimate by averaging them to get 1(4 + 2\sqrt2).
